newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's 1996 tax rate cut by Q4 benefit.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's 1996 tax rate cut by Q4 benefit.

text.p: McDonald's Corp said its effective income tax rate was unusually low in 1996 and in the fourth quarter due to a fourth quarter tax benefit.
For the year, the rate was 30.1 percent, compared with a 1995 rate of 34.2 percent. For the fourth quarter, the rate was 21.7 percent, versus 32.0 percent a year earlier.
"For 1997, the company expects the effective tax rate to be in the range of 32.5 to 33.5 percent," McDonald's said.
"The unusually low 1996 rates were primarily due to the $50 million tax benefit recorded in the fourth quarter," the company said.

Excluding the fourth-quarter benefit, the 1996 effective income tax rates for the year and fourth quarter would have been 32.4 and 31.2 percent, respectively, reflecting lower taxes related to foreign operations, McDonald's said.
